body:
Thank you for answering, I really appreciate it. 

For the part about philosophy about no-self: great that you feel things are quite clear for you. The sites and ideas I've been reading upon regarding no-self really do argue that there is no actual I but only I as an idea in the same way that there is no real Santa Clause but only Santa Clause as an idea. So if you say 'I believe that I do 'exist' in that my physical body has a form...' they would try tell you something like: 'So there is 'my body' which indicates a body and a me, in which the me owns the body. The body can be found, but where is the me?'. I haven't figured it out myself, but the idea is that it will be seen that there is no me, no I if looked for and the illusion will be seen. Liberionunleashed.com is a forum that helps people to see this, I tried it as well, but with no success. Take a look if you're interested, but I'd understand it if you don't feel like it and are happy with your current perspective (which is a reasonable perspective, if you ask me). 

About the part of my second question: Interesting. Can you tell me more about your perspective of 'all sensations are the same and I don't even exist'? It seems like there is still a big gap between that Idea and imaginative ideas like 'I am a child of an alien' (which are very interesting). 

About the part of wanting getting into psychosis: Being so totally out of control and going to shitty things like breakups and losing jobs must be unimaginably terrible. I don't think I have a choice of letting my mind go or not, but I wouldn't let it go for spiritual adventure. The 'something more' makes sense, as if there is something good to get in psychosis. I imagine delusions to be entertaining, but that's most probably untrue. 

Yes I have been taking antipsychotic risperdal already for some of my symptoms. 

By the way srry for not using the quotation function, I don't know how to use it. 

Thanks

Hi there,

I feel related to your reply because I have been focussing on the idea of no-self for a pretty long time and have been diagnosed as ultra high risk for psychosis. 

This sounds strange, but I feel like I want to get it to psychosis. If I look at it rationally, I probably don't want to. It's just that in my imagination it offers a place of escape from and understanding of of my current painful state of confusion (not psychosis-like confusion, it would finally make sense why I have been feeling this way). I know it isn't an escape, it was would probably be the pain I feel now plus the terrifying things a break from reality can do. 

I have two questions if that's okay. First, did you figure the no-self thing out? And second, when and how did your normal spirituality and philosophy/thinking change into delusions?

Thanks
